prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep a single-part B027 prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The scientific case is unchanged and was not weakened by anything said in round 1: proglucagon processing and the incretin effect, the insulinotropic action of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, receptor biology, and then drugs with independently replicated outcome benefit in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. The mechanism is stable and the recognition is neither premature nor contested on efficacy. All six of us converged on the same trio, but I treat that as a result of the arguments made, not as the argument. The chair asked whether a second part should be added. With a three-person cap, a second part would require cutting the GLP-1 part to one or two names, and each of Drucker, Holst and Mojsov carries a distinct step of the discovery chain, so I do not think the cap should be spent that way this year. I also keep the citation anchored in physiology and the active peptide, while saying explicitly that this physiology is what made incretin-based therapy possible, so that the omission of Knudsen is not read as dismissing drug development.
statement.case_against: The weakness is attribution, not merit. Mojsov's priority for identifying and synthesising the active peptide is disputed, Habener is outside the credited names and may have a comparable claim, and I cannot settle this from the supplied materials. Excluding Knudsen leaves out the person whose analogue design produced the drugs in use, so a physiology-anchored citation may look detached from the therapy that changed practice. Wahren-Herlenius is right that the discovery-versus-development principle should be decided openly and not be produced by the three-name limit. If the documentary record showed Mojsov's contribution to be unsupportable, I would reopen the third slot, but I would still consider the discovery-side candidates before Knudsen. A single-part prize also means a strong basic-science achievement such as B014 waits another year.

responses.point: The discovery-versus-development line should not be a hard rule, since the same logic would count against B036, which she ranks second because translation was the achievement. She asks that the principle be decided openly and that the configuration be presented as leaving out a contested contributor.
responses.response: This is a fair challenge and I accept it. My position is not that translation never counts. It is that in this case the discovery step, the physiology of the hormone and the identification of its active form, is separable from the optimisation of a molecule and has its own original content, whereas in B036 the translational proof of concept is the whole achievement and the TNF biology and antibody engineering sit outside the credited pair. I therefore apply the same test to both, namely what was discovered and who is credited for it, and I do not simply favour basic science. I agree we should say plainly that the trio leaves out Habener and Knudsen, who both have claims, and that the choice rests on a stated principle. Given that principle, I do not move B036 ahead of B014 or B039 as a second part.

responses.point: He wants the citation tied to discovery of the hormone's action rather than to a product, accepts that Mojsov is the least certain slot, and wants the documentary record on Mojsov and Habener examined before the final ballot.
responses.response: I agree on the citation scope and on the need for scrutiny of the record. Where I would go further is on the wording. A citation limited to physiology and the active peptide, with the phrase that it made incretin-based treatment possible, links discovery to therapy without crediting analogue design. His point on Eshhar in B039 also holds for my alternatives: I list B039 only as a fallback, because a prize for CAR design that skips the originators of the chimeric receptor concept would be open to a priority challenge, and the credit logic would have to be stated. I do not think my unease about Mojsov changes the ranking, because the alternative thirds have problems that I judge to be larger, not smaller.

responses.point: As chair he accepts B014 as strong and acceptable on basic science, would put it ahead of B036 on originality, and doubts that a chaperonin-folding prize adds much beyond it. He also observes that a single GLP-1 part leaves no space for a second achievement.
responses.response: I agree that if a second part were wanted, B014 is the cleanest and most original, and I agree it would add more than a chaperonin prize. My answer to his question on a two-part configuration is that the cap makes it a poor trade this year. Pairing B014 (Mori, Walter) with GLP-1 would leave one GLP-1 name, which would have to be Holst or Drucker, and either choice would break the physiology chain that the prize is meant to recognise. I would rather keep B014 as the first alternative than fragment B027. I also hold my earlier point that B001 does not match the scale of incretin therapy, which I think is consistent with his own view of it as a later candidate.

responses.point: He would pin the citation to the physiology and the active peptide, say explicitly that it does not extend to drug design, and keep Mojsov's priority from depending on a single originator.
responses.response: I agree with his reasoning on Habener and with pinning the citation to physiology and the active form, since that is the most defensible wording whatever the historical record shows. I differ slightly on whether to state that the citation excludes drug design. I would prefer to mention that the discoveries made incretin-based therapy possible, and not to add an explicit exclusion, because an explicit exclusion invites the reading that the committee set aside the therapeutic step. He is right that optogenetics is attractive but cannot be resolved among six names, and I share that view on B028.

responses.point: He would want the committee to see the record on the active GLP-1 fragment before the final ballot, and notes that priority disputes make Mojsov a less clean choice than Knudsen in some respects.
responses.response: I accept that Mojsov is less clean than Knudsen on priority and I do not dismiss it. The supplied materials do not settle the matter, and I cannot confirm the chronology independently. What I weigh is the nature of the claim. A contested priority for a discovery step is a different problem from a development contribution that is uncontested but is optimisation of a known molecule. For that reason I keep Mojsov while recording that her weight is the least certain element. I did not change my configuration in this round.

uncertainties: Whether the documentary record on the active GLP-1 peptide supports Mojsov over Habener, who is outside the credited names. I cannot resolve this from the supplied materials.
Whether the committee will accept a physiology-anchored citation that omits Knudsen, or will treat the therapeutic step as the achievement that changed medicine.
Whether a two-part configuration with B014 would be better than a single GLP-1 part, given that the cap would reduce GLP-1 to one name.
My knowledge of the discovery chronology is recollection and has not been independently checked.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. I have co-authored with Linnarsson and Frisen, and my research touches RNA processing and single-cell methods, but no shortlisted candidate involves a documented collaboration or institutional tie of mine. No recusal is needed.
